source: KPI Academy — Product Decisions & KPI Registry

kpis.name: Food Cost %
kpis.period: Matching reporting period and outlet scope
assumptions: Food inventory and purchases use the same valuation basis.
Transfers and adjustments are recorded separately.

kpis.name: Beverage Cost %
kpis.period: Matching reporting period and outlet scope
assumptions: Beverage inventory and purchases use the same valuation basis.
Transfers and adjustments are recorded separately.

kpis.name: COGS
kpis.period: Same inventory valuation basis and reporting period
assumptions: Transfers and adjustments must be separately recorded.

kpis.name: Labor Cost %
assumptions: Included wages, overtime, benefits and employer costs must follow outlet policy.

kpis.name: Prime Cost
assumptions: Use the same COGS and labor definitions as component KPIs.

kpis.name: Average Check
kpis.period: Same reporting period and outlet scope
assumptions: Use a consistent check-count definition; do not substitute covers.

kpis.name: Sales Mix %
kpis.formula: Unit Mix = Item Units ÷ Total Units × 100; Revenue Mix = Item Net Sales ÷ Total Net Sales × 100
assumptions: The mode must be explicitly selected and labeled as Unit Mix or Revenue Mix.

kpis.name: Contribution Margin
kpis.period: Same unit, currency and variable-cost basis

kpis.name: Break-even Sales
kpis.formula: Fixed Costs ÷ Contribution Margin Ratio; CM Ratio = Total Contribution Margin ÷ Net Sales
kpis.period: Matching reporting period and sales-mix assumptions
assumptions: Contribution-margin ratio must be positive and non-zero.

kpis.name: Inventory Turnover
kpis.formula: Period COGS ÷ Average Inventory; Average Inventory = (Opening + Closing) ÷ 2
kpis.period: Same reporting period and valuation basis
assumptions: Use a documented daily/monthly average instead when supplied.

kpis.name: Waste %
kpis.formula: Recorded Waste Cost ÷ Food & Beverage COGS × 100
assumptions: KPI Academy internal denominator; not a universal industry definition.

kpis.name: RevPASH
kpis.formula: Net F&B Revenue ÷ Available Seat Hours; Seat Hours = Available Seats × Operating Hours
assumptions: Adjust for seats or time unavailable during operations.
